cards.text: Friend, Amos, a prophet from Tekoa, has been bringing Israel some HEAVY news (Amos 1:1). God says He'll destroy the sinful kingdom and shake the house of Israel among all the nations, as grain is sifted in a sieve. But He also says He will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob.
Then the LORD looks ahead to 'that day,' and He talks about the tent of David. And friend, that tent is DOWN: gaps, ruins, the works.

cards.question: The tent of David has fallen, full of gaps and ruins. What does the LORD promise to do with it?

answers.text: Rebuild it as in the days of old
Leave it fallen as a warning
Fold it up and pack it away

cards.text: Repair the gaps, restore the ruins, rebuild the whole thing. That's not a touch-up, friend, that's the WHOLE renovation show, demo day to the big reveal.

cards.question: Once the tent of David is rebuilt, what does the LORD say they will possess?

answers.text: Edom's remnant and the nations bearing His name
Philistia's cities and the whole land of Moab
Egypt's fields and the faraway land of Cush

cards.question: The LORD says someone else will have to do the work of rebuilding the tent of David.

cards.text: He signs it right there: "declares the LORD, who will do this." Friend, that's the one contractor who never says 'I'll be back Tuesday' and then disappears for three weeks.
Then the LORD says, "Behold, the days are coming," and paints a picture of the farms. Get this: "the plowman will overtake the reaper."

cards.question: The plowman catches up to the reaper before the harvest is done. What does that tell you about the harvest?

answers.text: It's so big it never seems to end
It's so small it's over too fast
It's spoiled before anyone gathers it

cards.text: Same with the treader of grapes catching up to the sower of seed. That's me still pulling one batch out of the oven while the NEXT batch of dough is tapping me on the shoulder like, 'Papa. Papa. PAPA. We're READY.'

cards.question: With grapes coming in like that, the mountains will drip with sweet ___, and all the hills will flow with it.
Israel has been shaken out among the nations. Now the LORD says He will restore His people Israel from ___.
The LORD says the ruined cities won't stay that way. What will His people do with them?

answers.text: Rebuild them and live in them

cards.text: Then the LORD gets to the vineyards. Earlier in Amos, God warned Israel they wouldn't drink the wine from the vineyards they planted (Amos 5:11).

cards.question: This time, the LORD says His people will plant vineyards and drink their wine.

cards.text: Same with the gardens: they make them, and they eat their fruit. That's finishing the big project at work and actually getting the credit, with no coworker jumping in at the meeting like, 'Sooo, I had this idea…'
Then the LORD turns the planting picture onto His people themselves. He says, "I will firmly plant them in their own land."

cards.question: Firmly planted, the LORD says His people will never again be ___ from their land.
The LORD says the land Israel is planted in is land they won for themselves.

cards.text: It closes with "says the LORD your God," the last words of the whole book of Amos. Nine chapters of storm clouds, and the final word is a PROMISE, friend, and I'm over here crying into my apron like it's the end of a movie.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 8 quotes "the plowman will overtake the reaper.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 17 quotes "I will firmly plant them in their own land.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card calls Amos 'a prophet from Tekoa' and cites Amos 1:1. That verse calls him 'one of the sheepherders of Tekoa' and does not call him a prophet. In Amos 7:14 Amos says, 'I was not a prophet.'

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The right answer 'Rebuild it as in the days of old' uses Bible wording, so it stands out from the plain wrong answers. The wrong answer 'Fold it up and pack it away' also reads as silly.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The right answer sounds more like the Bible than the wrong answers.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The setup says 'Israel has been shaken out among the nations.' In Amos 9:9 the shaking is still future: 'I will shake the house of Israel among all the nations.' The setup also links the sifting in 9:9 to the captivity in 9:14, and the text does not make that link.

rule.text: When he connects two passages, or explains what a law was for, he says only what the texts state.

findings.problem: Saying the shaking has already happened changes the tense of Amos 9:9.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The question says the ruined cities 'won't stay that way.' That rules out the wrong answer 'Leave them to their enemies' before the baker reasons it through.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'Nine chapters of storm clouds' describes the whole book as nothing but judgment. Amos also calls people to seek the LORD and live (Amos 5:4, 5:6, 5:14), and chapter 9 itself contains this promise of restoration. The line is a description of Scripture, not one of Papa Dorin's own jokes.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.
